sources.query: GRAPH PaysimGraph MATCH (t:transaction) RETURN COUNT(*) AS landed
GRAPH PaysimGraph MATCH (t:transaction) RETURN ROUND(SUM(FLOAT64(t.amount))/1000000,2) AS volume_m

GRAPH PaysimGraph MATCH (t:transaction) RETURN ROUND(SUM(IF(BOOL(t.isfraud),FLOAT64(t.amount),0)),0) AS at_risk, ROUND(100*SUM(IF(BOOL(t.isfraud),FLOAT64(t.amount),0))/GREATEST(SUM(FLOAT64(t.amount)),1),2) AS pct_value, ROUND(MAX(IF(BOOL(t.isfraud),FLOAT64(t.amount),0)),0) AS biggest
GRAPH PaysimGraph MATCH (t:transaction) RETURN SUBSTR(STRING(t.timestamp),1,10) AS day, IF(BOOL(t.isfraud),'fraud','legitimate') AS kind, ROUND(SUM(FLOAT64(t.amount)),2) AS volume ORDER BY day

GRAPH PaysimGraph MATCH (t:transaction) RETURN CAST(FLOOR(LOG10(GREATEST(FLOAT64(t.amount),1))) AS INT64) AS decade, CASE CAST(FLOOR(LOG10(GREATEST(FLOAT64(t.amount),1))) AS INT64) WHEN 0 THEN 'under $10' WHEN 1 THEN '$10–99' WHEN 2 THEN '$100–999' WHEN 3 THEN '$1k–10k' WHEN 4 THEN '$10k–100k' ELSE '$100k+' END AS band, ROUND(100*COUNTIF(BOOL(t.isfraud))/COUNT(*),1) AS percent_fraud ORDER BY decade

GRAPH PaysimGraph MATCH (a:client)-[:has_ssn|has_email|has_phone]->(i)<-[:has_ssn|has_email|has_phone]-(b:client) WHERE a.id <> b.id RETURN i.id AS ident, COUNTIF(EXISTS { MATCH (x:client)-[:performs]->(t:transaction)-[:to_client]->(y:client) WHERE x.id = a.id AND y.id = b.id }) AS pairs NEXT RETURN IF(pairs > 0, 'ring confirmed', 'innocent so far') AS verdict, COUNT(*) AS identities

GRAPH PaysimGraph MATCH (c:client)-[:performs]->(t:transaction) WHERE BOOL(t.isfraud) RETURN STRING(c.name) AS suspect, COUNT(*) AS txns, ROUND(SUM(FLOAT64(t.amount)),2) AS moved ORDER BY moved DESC LIMIT 8

GRAPH PaysimGraph MATCH (a:client)-[:has_ssn|has_email|has_phone]->(i)<-[:has_ssn|has_email|has_phone]-(b:client) WHERE a.id <> b.id RETURN a.id AS aid, COUNT(*) AS shares NEXT MATCH (s:client)-[:performs]->(t:transaction)-[:to_client]->(r:client) WHERE s.id = aid RETURN STRING(r.name) AS collector, ROUND(SUM(FLOAT64(t.amount)),2) AS received ORDER BY received DESC LIMIT 8

GRAPH PaysimGraph MATCH (v:client)-[:performs]->(t:transaction)-[:to_client]->(m:client) WHERE STRING(m.client_type) = 'MULE' RETURN STRING(m.name) AS mule, ROUND(SUM(FLOAT64(t.amount)),2) AS taken ORDER BY taken DESC LIMIT 10

GRAPH PaysimGraph MATCH (t:transaction)-[:to_merchant]->(m:merchant) RETURN IF(BOOL(m.highrisk),'high-risk merchants','normal merchants') AS destination, 'merchant cash-out' AS channel, ROUND(SUM(FLOAT64(t.amount)),2) AS volume

widgets.title: Volume per simulated day — fraud stacked on top
Shared identities — how many are actually rings
Where money from identity-sharing accounts lands
% of each size band that is fraud
Reading this as an investigator
widgets.text:
**Money, not count.** The gauge is fraud as a share of *value*. By transaction count fraud is 0.27% — the number that makes it look like nothing. By value it is an order of magnitude worse, which is what a fraud desk is accountable for.

**Shared identity is a lead, not a verdict.** The left-hand chart splits the identities a flat rule flags into the ones where money actually moves between the holders and the ones where it never does. Identity edges load up front; the money arrives on the stream, so the "ring confirmed" bar grows from zero while the total stays put. The bar that does not grow is a family sharing a phone.

**Follow one name.** *Who moved the fraud money* is the case file — one account carries most of the value. Click any bar to select those nodes on the canvas and open the neighbourhood.
